blockers.quote: nine further trials, platform and basket designs, recruiting | defined by molecular alteration rather than histology  /  Nine further trials are molecularly rather than histologically defined and none lists this disease.
blockers.why: The nine are nine REGISTRY RECORDS for two trials, not nine trials. In research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json → task_2_widened_search.molecularly_defined_not_histology_defined, the `assessment` field of seven of the nine (NCT05768178, NCT05770037, NCT05770102, NCT05770544, NCT05786716, NCT06988475, NCT07440290) reads verbatim 'Arm of NCT05722886; admission is by genomic alteration, not histology.' NCT05722886 is the DETERMINE master screening protocol itself, so eight of the nine are one UK platform trial and its seven treatment-arm registrations; only NCT03767075 (Vall d'Hebron modular multi-basket) is a second independent trial. Counting arms as trials multiplies the apparent number of molecularly-defined options a patient has by roughly four, which is the same inflation the paper's own §3 refuses two paragraphs later ('A reachability claim that quietly counts an observational cohort alongside interventional trials inflates itself').
blockers.fix: Replace the table row and the abstract sentence with: 'Two further molecularly-defined trial programmes carry no histology in their conditions field — the DETERMINE platform trial (NCT05722886, registered as a master protocol plus seven treatment-arm records) and a modular multi-basket trial (NCT03767075) — so nine registry records in total, none of which names this disease.'

blockers.quote: The fetcher passed registry payloads through an HTML stripper, which deletes spans between angle brackets; the registry escapes comparison operators the same way, so eligibility text containing them lost characters.
blockers.why: The escaping mechanism is the version this repository measured and retracted. scripts/lit_fetch_urls.py, the comment block immediately above the fix (lines ~218-243), reads verbatim: '⚠ SUPERSEDED, RETAINED: this comment first said the trigger was HTML-ESCAPED brackets (`<`/`>`). That was wrong and the synthetic written from it did not reproduce the defect — modules survived. The real record settles it: 0 literal `<` and 13 orphaned literal `>` remain in the damaged file, which is the stripper's own footprint.' The same file's live text states the actual mechanism: 'ClinicalTrials.gov emits LITERAL angle brackets inside free-text eligibility criteria — "PLT < 100,000/mcL", "prednisone > 10 mg daily"'. The paper ships the refuted story to the one audience §6 addresses — people building retrieval tools.
blockers.fix: The fetcher passed registry payloads through an HTML stripper, which deletes everything from a `<` to the next `>`; the registry writes comparison operators as literal angle brackets inside eligibility text, so each one opened a span that swallowed whatever followed — in the worst case whole modules, leaving a record that still parsed.

The source key in research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json is task_2_widened_search.molecularly_defined_not_histology_defined — 'not histology defined', not 'admits' — and five of its nine entries carry eligibility_text_retrieved = false (NCT05768178, NCT05770037, NCT05770102, NCT05770544, NCT05786716, plus NCT07440290 = six). The artifact labels the arms explicitly: 'Arm of NCT05722886'. That is the same inflation the manuscript says it refuses two paragraphs later ('A reachability claim that quietly counts an observational cohort alongside interventional trials inflates itself').
blockers.fix: Replace the row with: '| two further molecularly defined studies — one platform trial with seven registered arms (one not yet recruiting) and one multi-basket trial | candidates only: identified from fielded screens with no eligibility text retrieved, so admission is unconfirmed and the open arms are defined on ALK, BRAF, ROS1, MET, HER2 and TMB/MSI rather than on this fusion | various; none names this histology | no |'

blockers.quote: The rule applied at the time was that no sentence carrying a removal marker may be quoted. That defect has since been fixed at the fetcher.
blockers.why: The paragraph reads as a complete disposal of the transport defect and is not. Of the two headline interventional trials, NCT05918640 was read only through the defective transport and was never re-fetched afterwards: research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> task_2_widened_search.confirmed_fusion_family_defined[0] records removal_markers_in_eligibility_text = 1 for it, and research/literature/emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json -> adjudications covers only NCT06571734, NCT04151342, NCT06094101 and NCT07188532. The adjudication artifact's own transport_integrity block describes the silent mode as 'a record that still parses while whole modules have vanished', and section 4 of this manuscript demonstrates the exact failure this matters for — NCT06094101 is fusion-framed in its title and histology-restricted in a criterion sentence. A restricting clause lost to the stripper in NCT05918640 would not have been detectable by the quoting rule, because the manuscript quotes nothing from that trial.
blockers.fix: Replace with: 'The rule applied at the time was that no sentence carrying a removal marker may be quoted. That defect has since been fixed at the fetcher, and the four candidates adjudicated on 2026-08-09 were re-fetched through the fixed path; the FET-family trial was not, so its eligibility reading still rests on a payload that carried one removal marker and should be re-read before the claim is relied on.'

blockers.quote: Sponsors whose eligibility is molecular should list the histologies that criterion admits, or the molecular class itself, in the conditions field.
blockers.why: The paper's own second exemplar already complies with the second half of this remedy and is still counted as unreachable, so the remedy would not fix the case it is offered for. research/literature/emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json -> adjudications[0].listed_conditions for NCT06571734 contains the exact string 'Translocation-associated Soft Tissue Sarcoma' — the molecular class the admitting cohort is defined on is already in the conditions field. The manuscript's abstract conceals this by enumerating only part of the field: 'its listed conditions name leiomyosarcoma, synovial sarcoma and osteosarcoma', omitting 'Translocation-associated Soft Tissue Sarcoma', 'Bone Sarcoma' and 'Ewing Sarcoma'. Section 1's mechanism statement carries the same overreach — 'the class is named in the criteria and the disease is not named anywhere' — when for this trial the class is named in the index as well. Either listing the class is a sufficient remedy, in which case NCT06571734 is not evidence of the problem, or it is not, in which case remedy 1 must not offer it.
blockers.fix: Replace with: 'Sponsors whose eligibility is molecular should list the histologies that criterion admits, and not the molecular class alone: the zanzalintinib trial already lists translocation-associated soft tissue sarcoma among its conditions, and a patient who searches their own histology still does not reach it.'

blockers.quote: A registry-wide term search for it returns five studies (exercise physiology, spinal-cord injury, neck pain, and a surgical cholangiocarcinoma series) that mention the gene incidentally. Not one is an oncology study.
blockers.why: The sentence contradicts itself, and the same contradiction is carried into the abstract ('returns five studies, not one of which is an oncology study'). The parenthetical names a cholangiocarcinoma resection series, and research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> task_2_widened_search.nr4a3_is_absent_from_the_registry_index.studies[0] is NCT00733200, brief_title 'Surgical Treatment of Hilar Cholangiocarcinoma: Minor or Major Liver Resection?', listed_conditions ['Cholangiocarcinoma', 'Surgical Treatment', 'Hepatectomy'], intervention 'Minor or Major Liver Resection' — a study of cancer surgery in patients with a registered malignancy. The artifact's own 'finding' string carries the identical error and is not independent evidence for it. The claim the paper actually needs is about indexing, not about specialty, and it survives intact once stated correctly; as written, a referee reading one sentence finds it refuted by its own parenthesis.
blockers.fix: Replace with: 'A registry-wide term search for it returns five studies — two exercise-physiology trials, one spinal-cord-injury trial, one neck-pain trial and one cholangiocarcinoma resection series — each of which mentions the gene incidentally. None is a study of this disease, and none is indexed to it.'

blockers.where: research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md — Abstract, 'What we found'; and §4.1, final paragraph
blockers.quote: where the disease is named in a registry, it is named in order to exclude it. ... [§4.1] Where trials are indexed by histology, this disease appears only as an exclusion; where they are indexed molecularly, it is admitted and never named. In neither case does a search of the diagnosis return a trial the patient could join.
blockers.why: The paper's own supporting artifact contains a counter-example in the registry the paper measured first. research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json → task_1_reverification_of_section_3_3.trials[1] is NCT06239272 (NRSTS2021, St. Jude): overall_status 'RECRUITING', phases ['PHASE1','PHASE2'], interventions include Pazopanib/Selinexor/doxorubicin (a treatment trial), listed_conditions contains the literal string 'Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma', emc_in_listed_conditions = true, and memo_claim_checked reads 'verified open and EMC-eligible; EMC an explicitly listed condition'. Two further records in the same file name the histology inclusively in their conditions: trials[6] NCT05836571 ('Locally Advanced Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma', ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING) and trials[7] NCT03600649 ('Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma', status UNKNOWN). So in ClinicalTrials.gov the disease IS named in order to admit, and a condition search of the diagnosis DOES return a recruiting interventional trial the patient could join (subject to that trial's maximum_age of 30 Years, which the paper also never states). The universal as written is refuted by the file the paper cites for its own counts.
blockers.fix: Replace with: 'In the US registry the disease is named in the conditions field of three trials and admitted by them, one of which — NCT06239272, recruiting, ages up to 30 — is findable by a diagnosis search; in the one non-US registry that answered, the only record naming the disease names it in order to exclude it. The two trials in §3 are the ones that admit WITHOUT naming, and they are the mechanism this paper reports; they are not the whole of what a diagnosis search returns.'

blockers.where: research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md — §3 table, third row; and Abstract, 'What we found'
blockers.quote: nine further trials, platform and basket designs, recruiting | defined by molecular alteration rather than histology | various; none names this histology | no
blockers.why: Nine is a count of registry RECORDS, not of trials, and the artifact says so record by record. research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json → task_2_widened_search.molecularly_defined_not_histology_defined holds exactly 9 entries; NCT05722886 is the DETERMINE 'Master Screening Protocol', and seven of the remaining eight (NCT05768178, NCT05770037, NCT05770102, NCT05770544, NCT05786716, NCT06988475, NCT07440290) each carry the field assessment = 'Arm of NCT05722886; admission is by genomic alteration, not histology.' Eight of the nine are therefore one platform trial. Only NCT03767075 (Basket of Baskets) is a second, independent trial. The row also labels all nine 'recruiting', but NCT07440290 has overall_status = 'NOT_YET_RECRUITING' in the same file. The inflation is load-bearing: the paper argues in §4.1 that this is 'a disease where the number of options is small enough that each one carries weight', so a 9-for-2 count of options misstates the quantity the paper's own argument turns on.
blockers.fix: Replace the row with: 'two further trials registered as nine records — the DETERMINE platform (NCT05722886 plus seven treatment arms, one of them not yet recruiting) and one basket study — defined by molecular alteration rather than histology; none names this histology.'

blockers.where: research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md — Abstract, 'What we did'; and §2, final paragraph
blockers.quote: We read one public registry twice and a second one once, retrieving the full eligibility text of every candidate individually rather than trusting a fielded screen. ... [§2] Every claim below therefore rests on a per-trial retrieval, and the two refusals in §4 were only detectable that way.
blockers.why: Six of the nine records in §3's third row have eligibility_text_retrieved = false in research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json → task_2_widened_search.molecularly_defined_not_histology_defined: NCT05768178, NCT05770037, NCT05770102, NCT05770544, NCT05786716 and NCT07440290. Each of those carries retrieved_from.payload = 'ct_basket_recruiting_fixed', whose source_url ends '&fields=NCTId%7CBriefTitle%7COverallStatus%7CPhase%7CInterventionName%7CCondition%7CStudyType' — i.e. precisely the fielded screen the abstract says was not trusted, and which §2 itself says 'can identify a candidate and can never confirm one'. Their eligibility_basis ('molecularly defined DETERMINE arm') is inferred from the arm title, not read from criteria. The methods claim states a stronger evidence base than the record supports for two thirds of one of the three rows.
blockers.fix: Replace with: 'We read one public registry twice and a second one once. Every trial we adjudicate as admitting or refusing this disease had its full eligibility text retrieved individually; the platform arms counted in §3 were identified from a fields-limited screen that carries no eligibility text, and are reported as identified rather than confirmed.'

blockers.where: research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md — §3, final paragraph; and Abstract, 'What we found'
blockers.quote: A registry-wide term search for it returns five studies (exercise physiology, spinal-cord injury, neck pain, and a surgical cholangiocarcinoma series) that mention the gene incidentally. Not one is an oncology study.
blockers.why: The sentence contradicts itself, and the record confirms the contradiction rather than the claim. research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json → task_2_widened_search.nr4a3_is_absent_from_the_registry_index.studies[0] is NCT00733200, 'Surgical Treatment of Hilar Cholangiocarcinoma: Minor or Major Liver Resection?', listed_conditions = ['Cholangiocarcinoma', 'Surgical Treatment', 'Hepatectomy'], an interventional study in a malignancy. That is an oncology study. The defensible absence is narrower: none of the five is a sarcoma study and none is indexed to this disease.
blockers.fix: Replace with: 'A registry-wide term search for it returns five studies — two exercise-physiology trials, one spinal-cord-injury trial, one neck-pain trial and one hilar-cholangiocarcinoma surgical series — every one of which mentions the gene incidentally and none of which is a sarcoma study or is indexed to this disease.'

blockers.quote: The other has a cohort for *translocation-associated soft tissue sarcoma*, which EMC is; its listed conditions name leiomyosarcoma, synovial sarcoma and osteosarcoma.
blockers.why: The enumeration drops the one listed condition that decides the contrast the sentence is drawing. In research/literature/emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json → adjudications[0] (NCT06571734), listed_conditions = ['Metastatic Leiomyosarcoma','Unresectable Leiomyosarcoma','Bone Sarcoma','Translocation-associated Soft Tissue Sarcoma','Synovial Sarcomas','Osteosarcoma Metastatic','Ewing Sarcoma'] — the molecular class term IS in the conditions field. The same is recorded independently in research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json → task_2_widened_search.candidates_requiring_eligibility_text_verification[0], whose eligibility_basis field reads 'listed condition is itself translocation-defined'. The abstract's contrast (molecular in the criteria, histological in the index) is therefore manufactured by omission for this exemplar; §3's table carries the term but the abstract does not. It also silently undercuts §6 Remedy 1, which asks sponsors to list 'the molecular class itself, in the conditions field' — a thing this trial already does.
blockers.fix: Replace with: 'The other has a cohort for *translocation-associated soft tissue sarcoma*, which EMC is, and it does list that class term among its conditions alongside leiomyosarcoma, synovial sarcoma, Ewing sarcoma and osteosarcoma — so it is reachable by a class search and still invisible to a search of the diagnosis, which names no histology this patient has.'

blockers.where: research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md — §5 Limitations, third bullet; and §2 table, third row ('four endpoints attempted, one answered')
blockers.quote: A non-US sweep ran on the date of this draft and only one of four non-US endpoints answered. The EU endpoint returned an authentication error for the second time on a second date, and two more refused automated access. The WHO portal was not reached because this sweep's URL was wrong, a defect here rather than a finding about that registry.
blockers.why: The denominator contradicts the enumeration in its own sentence and the artifact. research/literature/non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json → endpoints lists six entries, of which five are non-US: ISRCTN (HTTP 200, read), WHO ICTRP (HTTP 404, our own wrong URL), EU CTIS (HTTP 403), ANZCTR (HTTP 403) and jRCT (SSL handshake failure); ClinicalTrials.gov is flagged role = 'positive control'. The paper's own bullet then enumerates one answered + EU + 'two more' + WHO = five. Five non-US endpoints were attempted and one answered, not four. §2's table row repeats the wrong figure.
blockers.fix: Replace with: 'A non-US sweep ran on the date of this draft and only one of five non-US endpoints answered. The EU endpoint returned an authentication error for the second time on a second date, and two more refused automated access. The WHO portal was not reached because this sweep's URL was wrong, a defect here rather than a finding about that registry.' — and change §2's table cell to 'five endpoints attempted, one answered'.

blockers.where: research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md — §3, final paragraph (and the abstract's 'The sharpest result is an absence')
blockers.quote: No trial anywhere in that registry is indexed to this disease's driver.
blockers.why: This is a registry-wide universal, and the instrument behind it is not documented as enumerative. The result comes from research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json → task_2_widened_search.nr4a3_is_absent_from_the_registry_index, whose search_url is 'https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies?query.term=NR4A3&pageSize=100&format=json' — full records, pageSize=100 — and which records five studies and NO total count field. The same file's limits_of_this_screen[0] says of the identically-shaped sibling query: 'The registry-wide EWSR1 term search returns full records and is therefore capped by response size, not by pageSize: 7 studies came back for pageSize=100. It is a sample of EWSR1-indexed trials, not an enumeration.' Nothing committed establishes that the NR4A3 response was not truncated the same way, so the paper converts an un-bounded sample into an absolute absence — the one claim it calls its sharpest result. THE ONE OBSERVATION THAT SETTLES IT: re-run the query fields-limited (or record the payload's totalCount) and show the total equals 5; the claim is then earned as written.
blockers.fix: Replace with: 'A registry-wide term search for the driver gene returned five studies and no oncology study indexed to it. The search returns full records and is capped by response size rather than by page size, so it is a sample rather than an enumeration; what it establishes is that the driver gene surfaces no trial about this disease, not that no such record exists.'

p1s.what: No committed instrument binds any number, NCT identifier or trial status in this paper to the artifact that produced it. research/manuscripts/claim-coverage.json records this paper as `sentences: 69, covered: 0, with_a_number: 8, with_a_number_covered: 0, uncovered_with_a_number: 8`. `git grep NCT06571734` and `git grep NCT05918640` at this pin return no test, linter or schema — only the two literature JSONs, the manuscript, research/IDEAS.md and two other prose documents. research/manuscripts/pinned-figures.json lists the file path under `targets` but pins no figure from it. So n = 73, n = 5500, 'nine further trials', 'five studies', 'two trials', 'four endpoints' and every trial status could each be edited to any other value and the whole commit loop would stay green.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: Five of the eight numeric sentences are correct at this pin as written; four of the blockers above are exactly what an instrument on these eight sentences would have caught, which is the argument for the guard rather than a second defect.

p1s.what: Every trial status in the paper is a snapshot of `overall_status` on 2026-08-07 / 2026-08-09, and nothing in the repository re-reads them or records when they were last re-read. §5 discloses the staleness in prose, but the paper carries no retrieval date next to any individual status, so a reader cannot tell how old any one row is without reconstructing it from §2's table.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: The statuses match their artifacts at the pin (with the single exception filed as B2), and §5 makes the staleness explicit; the gap is that nothing will make the paper go red as the registry moves.

p1s.what: No committed guard binds this manuscript's identifiers to any artifact. `research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_manuscripts_gene_identifiers_are_ones_an_artifact_names.py` — the repository's identifier-provenance guard — scopes itself to the ASO deposit via `research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-archive-manifest.json`, and at the pin no file under research/manuscripts/tests or scripts contains the string 'care-delivery'. A single-character edit turning NCT06571734 into NCT06571743, or NR4A3 into NR4A7, would pass preflight, lint_citations and lint_claims unchanged. This is the exact defect class that guard's own docstring was written for, in the paper where a drifted NCT id is worst.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: Every NCT id, gene symbol and quoted criterion in the paper as it stands at the pin does appear in a committed artifact — I checked all of them. The gap is that nothing would catch the next edit.

p1s.what: Every structured field in the table — phase, status, enrolment (n = 73, n = 5500), and the listed-conditions enumerations — is hand-transcribed from the JSON with nothing comparing the two. The artifacts also carry `status_verified_date` values (NCT06571734: '2026-06'; NCT05918640: '2026-03') that the table does not surface, so a status that goes stale in the record cannot be detected from the paper. A guard asserting each table cell against its artifact field would have caught B4's 'recruiting' and P2-a's missing condition mechanically.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: Graded here as coverage; the specific transcription errors it would have caught are filed as B4 and P2-a.

p1s.what: No guard binds any number, status or identifier in this paper to the artifacts that produce them. pinned-figures.json lists the paper at targets[14] but has no entry for it in artifact_figures (99 entries, 0 matching this paper or any of its three source JSONs), derivations, table_completeness or subset_checks. claim-coverage.json records this paper as 69 sentences, covered 0, with_a_number 8, with_a_number_covered 0. So 'five studies', 'nine further trials', 'n = 73', 'n = 5500', 'four endpoints', every NCT identifier and every recruitment status can be edited, or drift in the registry, with nothing going red. Pin at least the five counts and the recruitment statuses to their artifact fields.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: The gap is in repository tooling, not in the outgoing text — but B1, B2 and B4 are all instances of exactly what this gap fails to catch, so it is the highest-value P1 here.

p1s.what: 'That defect has since been fixed at the fetcher' is true at the pin — scripts/lit_fetch_urls.py now routes JSON payloads around strip_html, with the reasoning in the comment block at lines 218-247 — but nothing ties the sentence to the code. A refactor that reinstated strip_html over JSON would falsify a published methods claim silently. A test asserting that a JSON content-type is never passed through strip_html would close it.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: The sentence is correct as of the pinned tree; only a future edit would make it false.

p1s.what: Not one claim in this manuscript is bound to a guard. research/manuscripts/claim-coverage.json records for 'research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md': sentences 69, covered 0, with_a_number 8, with_a_number_covered 0, uncovered 69. Every count the paper turns on — two interventional trials, nine further trials, five NR4A3 studies, n = 73, n = 5500, four non-US endpoints, two ISRCTN trials — is typed prose with nothing tying it to the JSON that produced it, and the paper does not appear in research/manuscripts/pinned-figures.json under any of those numbers (grep for NCT06571734 and NCT05918640 there returns zero hits).
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: The bound numbers I could re-derive are individually correct at this pin (n = 73 matches estimated_enrollment for NCT06571734; n = 5500 matches NCT04151342; the NR4A3 term search does return exactly five studies). The defect is that any future edit or artifact refresh silently falsifies them.

p1s.what: Recruitment statuses are typed into the section 3 table ('recruiting' on four rows) with no link to the overall_status field of the record that carries them, and the artifacts already record staleness that will make one of them wrong: research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> molecularly_defined_not_histology_defined for NCT03767075 says 'its RECRUITING flag is over two years stale in the registry - confirm directly with the site' (status_verified_date 2024-04). Section 5's generic 'Statuses go stale' is the only thing standing between this paper and a wrong status claim.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: Each status except NCT07440290's (see B3) matches the artifact at this pin, so the text is correct now; the gap is that nothing regenerates or checks it.

p1s.what: The paper appears in pinned-figures.json only in `targets` (the list of files lint_consistency scans). It has ZERO entries in `artifact_figures`: a search of that block for 'emc-trial-reachability' returns 0 hits, against 99 entries for other papers. So none of this paper's counts — the two admitting trials, the nine molecular records, the five NR4A3 studies, n = 73, n = 5500, the three refusals, the two ISRCTN hits — is bound to a field in the JSON that produced it. Re-running either sweep, or an ordinary prose edit, changes any of these numbers with nothing going red.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: The pin registry is repository tooling, not the outgoing artifact; the numbers that ARE currently correct stay correct until something edits them. It is the coverage gap that makes B2, B4 and B6 possible and undetectable, not itself a wrong statement to a reader.

p1s.what: No test module at the pin binds this paper to its two source JSONs. `git ls-tree research/manuscripts/tests/` returns no module naming this paper, this route or trial reachability (the only 'reach' match is test_the_canonical_file_third_state_is_reachable.py, which is about a different thing entirely). In particular nothing asserts that every NCT id in §3's table still carries the overall_status the table prints, which is the field the artifacts themselves warn goes stale — one of the nine is already NOT_YET_RECRUITING (B2) and NCT03767075's RECRUITING flag is recorded as over two years unverified.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: It is a missing guard in the repository's own test tier, not a claim a reader acts on.

note: Round 1. Five blind seats, five lenses, five independent sessions on the pinned commit. Blockers were applied to the prose in commits after this pin, so this record describes the round, not the repaired text; a round 2 at the repaired commit is required before clause 1 can clear.
